title: Paranormal narration to rap/electronic sounds: it gives us Chills!
excerpt: Chills, a member of Manitoba’s Minegoziibe Anishinabe, is bringing ten years of experience to his music. Known online as Number 15 for his horror and paranormal narrations, he blends rap, pop…
content:
Chills, a member of Manitoba’s Minegoziibe Anishinabe, is bringing ten years of experience to his music. Known online as Number 15 for his horror and paranormal narrations, he blends rap, pop, and electronic sounds. After the recent National Music Centre incubator in Calgary, he’s recording singles and working toward his second studio album. Here he is, in conversation with CKLB’s Stacie Arden Smith:

Chills: “My name is Chills. I’m a member of the Minegoziibe Anishinabe in Manitoba near Lake Winnipegosis.”

CKLB: “You are here as one of the seven artists that are at the OHSOTO’KINO incubator program over at the National Music Center. How has this experience been?”

Chills: “I’m just incredibly grateful for this experience. I think it’s been very humbling. I’ve learned so much throughout the week. I think it’s pushed me out of my comfort zone. I think just the insight, the support, the love of the other artists, the talent in the room —it’s just given me a new, like a new, a new look on music and a new way I want to approach my music. And it’s just motivated me where I’m just trying to get up to the level that some of these other artists are.”

CKLB: “Amazing! And what kind of music do you create?”

Chills: “So I create a combination of rap, pop, and electronic music. To some extent, melodic rap is the term I like to use, but it’s essentially a blend of those three genres,”

CKLB: “And to my understanding, this is not your first gig in the entertainment area. You have other talents. How has those experiences helped you for this music career?”

Chills: “I think it’s taught me that hard work is the means to success. The only way to get better at something is to just keep working at it. I think we all start from we all start from the same place when it comes to any sort of any sort of like artistic medium or anything that we want to get better at. I mean, it could be sports.

“It could be just you know trying to just have a good routine at home. We all start from you know square one, and we have to just keep working at it, moving forward. Try to stay disciplined. It’s the only way to improve. So, I music has been a really big passion of mine for a long time, and I think it’s attending things like this incubator that has shown me how important it is to pursue passions and really just hone in on my craft.”

CKLB: “And so that our audience kind of understands what I’m referring to, what is your previous career or is still part of your career?”

Chills: “For those who know, I’ll just say number 15. I’ve been making YouTube videos since I was in high school in the horror, true crime, scary paranormal genre. I’m quite well known for my narrations. Yeah, it’s been a blast on YouTube. I love it so much. I’ve been doing it now for over 10 years. Ever since I graduated high school, I’ve been you know blessed enough to do it full time, and I think it’s situations like that that have you know allowed me the ability to you know pursue something like music and just trying to get better at it and to participate in something like this incubator, and I was I was the baby of the group. I was the youngest one here, and I’d say the least experienced when it came to music. And everyone just welcomed me with open arms, and were so supportive. And I feel like just even already this week, I’ve seen so much improvement, and I feel I feel more confident within myself and my music.”

CKLB: “Well, you definitely blew us away with the showcase, and we had no idea that was your second performance, live performance. So, we had no clue whatsoever. And moving forward, what can we see from you? Is there any new music that’s coming forward, or are you in the midst of recording?”

Chills: “I’ve been working on new music throughout the course of the year. I released my first studio album, Sawiskera, in December of 2025, and my goal is to just keep recording music for the time being. I want to start releasing singles and hopefully start moving up towards creating, finishing, and releasing a second album that I’m happy with and you know ready to share with the world.”

CKLB: “Perfect. Well, we are completely excited to hear what comes from you because it sounded amazing all weekend long, and it has been an absolute treat getting to meet you.”

Chills: “Thank you so much, and likewise, it’s been great meeting you, Stacy. You’re incredibly talented yourself. I’ve learned so much from you during this week, and I just really appreciate it. And I just want to say a quick shout out to the Northwest Territories. I hope to be up there soon. I’ve always wanted to visit.”

CKLB: “Well, definitely now you know I live there, so by all means, give me a ring. You have a place to stay.”

Chills: “You’re gonna be the first person I call.”

CKLB: “Mahsi Cho”

Stacie Arden Smith/ Local Journalism Initiative reporter/ Native Communications Society
